fullPassage:
In a small town known for its flourishing academic community, two brothers, James and Daniel Carter, stood out for their exceptional effort and talent. James and his younger brother, Daniel, both applied for the Spark Fellowship. The Spark Fellowship was a highly respected program that selects and supports outstanding students every two years. Unsurprisingly, both brothers advanced to the final round.
Without Daniel knowing, James went to the selection committee. He told the committee, "Daniel has always been the more dedicated and talented one. He will excel in this program like no one else." Meanwhile, Daniel had the same idea as his older brother. He believed that his brother was the more ideal and deserving candidate. He also decided to visit and speak to the committee.
However, the program had a strict rule: only one family member could be selected in the same year. This posed a challenge to the selection committee, who thought it almost impossible to choose between the two equally impressive candidates. The committee gathered together, struggling all day long to decide. When James found out about this rule, he tried to seek a way to demonstrate Daniel's exceptional talent to the selection committee.
Not long after James had left, Daniel showed up at the selection committee and advocated for his brother, saying "James' leadership and vision make him the perfect choice. He deserves this chance more than I do." Moved by their selflessness, the committee made an exception by selecting both brothers in the same year, for the first time in its history. Their story inspired others, showing that true success lies not only in individual achievements but also in supporting and encouraging others.

questions.passage: In a small town known for its flourishing academic community, two brothers stood out for their exceptional effort and talent. James and his younger brother, Daniel, both ①<u>applied</u> for the Spark Fellowship. The Spark Fellowship was a highly respected program that selects and supports outstanding students. Unsurprisingly, both brothers ②<u>advanced</u> to the final round. Without Daniel ③<u>knew</u>, James went to the selection committee. He told the committee about Daniel's talent and ④<u>dedication</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ knew → knowing: 'Without + 목적어 + -ing' 분사구문.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ knew → knowing: Without + O + -ing (분사구문)
✅ ① applied: 과거시제 — 정상
❌ ② advanced: 과거시제 — 정상
❌ ④ dedication: 명사 — 정상
det.tip: Without + O + -ing: ~가 ~하지 않은 채. Without Daniel knowing = Daniel이 모르는 채

questions.passage: This posed a challenge to the selection committee, ①<u>who</u> thought it almost impossible to choose between the two equally impressive candidates. The committee gathered together, ②<u>struggling</u> all day long to decide. When James found out about this rule, he tried to seek a way ③<u>demonstrating</u> Daniel's exceptional talent. Not long after James ④<u>had left</u>, Daniel showed up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ demonstrating → to demonstrate: 'a way to V' 구조에서 to부정사 필요.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ a way to demonstrate: to부정사의 형용사적 용법
✅ ① who: 선행사 committee 수식 관계대명사 — 정상
✅ ② struggling: 분사구문 — 정상
✅ ④ had left: 대과거 — 정상
det.tip: a way to V = ~하는 방법. to부정사가 명사(way)를 수식

questions.passage: Daniel showed up at the selection committee and advocated for his brother, ①<u>saying</u> "James' leadership and vision make him the perfect choice. He ②<u>deserves</u> this chance more than I do." ③<u>Moving</u> by their selflessness, the committee made an exception by selecting both brothers. Their story inspired others, ④<u>showing</u> that true success lies in supporting others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ Moving → Moved: 위원회가 감동을 '받은'(수동) 것이므로 과거분사.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ Moving → Moved: 감정 수동태. 주어(committee)가 감동 받는 쪽
✅ ① saying: 분사구문 (동시동작) — 정상
✅ ② deserves: 직접화법 내 현재시제 — 정상
✅ ④ showing: 결과 분사구문 — 정상
det.tip: Moved by(감동받아) vs Moving(감동을 주는): 주어가 감동을 받으면 과거분사

questions.passage: In a small town known for its flourishing academic community, two brothers stood out for their exceptional effort. Both applied for the Spark Fellowship. Without Daniel knowing, James went to the committee. He told them, "Daniel has always been the more dedicated and talented one. He will excel in this program." Meanwhile, Daniel had the same idea. He believed that his brother was the more ideal and deserving candidate. However, the program had a ①<u>strict</u> rule: only one family member could be selected. The committee thought it almost impossible to choose between the two equally ②<u>impressive</u> candidates. When James found out about this rule, he tried to ③<u>hide</u> Daniel's talent from the committee. Moved by their ④<u>selflessness</u>, the committee made an exception.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ hide(숨기다) → demonstrate(보여주다): James는 Daniel의 재능을 위원회에 보여주려 한 것이지 숨기려 한 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ hide → demonstrate: 동생을 추천하는 맥락에서 재능을 '보여주려' 함
✅ ① strict: 엄격한 규칙 — 적절
✅ ② impressive: 인상적인 후보 — 적절
✅ ④ selflessness: 이타심 — 적절
det.tip: demonstrate(보여주다)↔hide(숨기다): 맥락상 James는 Daniel을 도우려는 것

questions.passage: Not long after James had left, Daniel showed up at the selection committee and ①<u>advocated</u> for his brother, saying "James' leadership and vision make him the ②<u>perfect</u> choice. He deserves this chance more than I do." Moved by their selflessness, the committee made an exception by selecting both brothers. Their story ③<u>inspired</u> others, showing that true success lies not only in individual achievements but also in ④<u>competing</u> with others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ competing(경쟁하는) → supporting and encouraging(돕고 격려하는): 원문의 교훈은 타인을 돕는 것이지 경쟁이 아니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ competing → supporting and encouraging: 이타심의 교훈과 '경쟁'은 모순
✅ ① advocated: 형을 옹호 — 적절
✅ ② perfect: 완벽한 선택 — 적절
✅ ③ inspired: 영감을 주었다 — 적절
det.tip: supporting and encouraging(돕고 격려하는)↔competing(경쟁하는): 글의 교훈은 양보/이타심

questions.passage: Without Daniel knowing, James went to the selection committee and told them Daniel was the more dedicated candidate. Meanwhile, Daniel had the same idea and also visited the committee to recommend James. However, the program had a strict rule: only one family member could be selected in the same year. This posed a challenge to the committee, who thought it almost impossible to choose. The question was: only one family member could be __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: selected in essentially the same year

det.korean: 같은 해에 한 가족에서 한 명만 선발될 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① selected in the same year: 원문의 규칙과 일치
❌ ② 리더십 직위 승진: 맥락과 무관
❌ ③ 학교 입학: fellowship 선발 맥락
❌ ④ 매년 장학금: 2년마다 선발
det.tip: the program had a strict rule = 프로그램에 엄격한 규칙이 있었다

questions.passage: In a small town, two brothers both applied for the Spark Fellowship. Without knowing each other's actions, each secretly recommended the other to the committee. Despite a strict one-per-family rule, the committee, moved by their selflessness, selected both brothers. Their story showed that true success requires not just talent but also __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the willingness to put others before oneself

det.korean: 진정한 성공에는 재능뿐 아니라 타인을 자신보다 앞세우려는 의지도 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② the willingness to put others before oneself: 형제의 이타적 행동을 요약
❌ ① 치열한 가족 경쟁: 이타심과 반대
❌ ③ 규칙 엄수: 위원회가 예외를 만듦
❌ ④ 고급 학력: 본문 핵심이 아님
det.tip: put others before oneself = 타인을 자기보다 앞세우다 = selflessness의 핵심

questions.passage: In a small town known for its flourishing academic community, two brothers, James and Daniel Carter, stood out for their exceptional effort and talent. James and his younger brother, Daniel, both applied for the Spark Fellowship. The Spark Fellowship was a highly respected program that selects and supports outstanding students every two years.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Spark Fellowship은 한 해에 수백 명을 선발한다.

det.korean: Spark Fellowship은 2년마다(every two years) 학생을 선발.
det.analysis:
✅ ② every two years와 일치
❌ ① 다른 학교: 언급 없음
❌ ③ Daniel이 형: James가 형(older brother)
❌ ④ 수백 명: 언급 없음
det.tip: every two years = 2년마다. 선지의 세부 정보가 원문과 일치하는지 확인

questions.passage: Without Daniel knowing, James went to the selection committee. He told the committee, "Daniel has always been the more dedicated and talented one. He will excel in this program like no one else." Meanwhile, Daniel had the same idea as his older brother. He believed that his brother was the more ideal and deserving candidate. He also decided to visit and speak to the committee.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Daniel은 James가 위원회를 방문한 사실을 알고 있었다.
James는 Daniel이 더 헌신적이라고 위원회에 말했다.
Daniel은 형이 더 자격 있는 후보라고 믿었다.
두 형제는 서로 상의 없이 같은 행동을 했다.

det.korean: ① 'Without Daniel knowing'이므로 Daniel은 James의 방문을 몰랐다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 불일치: Without Daniel knowing = 모르는 상태
✅ ② 일치: 'the more dedicated and talented one'
❌ ③ 일치: 'the more ideal and deserving candidate'
❌ ④ 일치: 서로 모른 채 같은 행동
det.tip: Without + O + -ing = ~가 모른 채. Daniel은 James의 행동을 몰랐다

questions.passage:

This posed a challenge to the selection committee, who thought it almost impossible to choose between the two equally impressive candidates. Not long after James had left, Daniel showed up at the selection committee and advocated for his brother. Moved by their selflessness, the committee made an exception by selecting both brothers in the same year, for the first time in its history.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 위원회는 두 후보 사이에서 쉽게 결정을 내렸다.
James는 프로그램의 규칙을 처음부터 알고 있었다.
위원회는 역사상 처음으로 두 형제를 모두 선발했다.
Daniel은 James가 떠나기 전에 위원회에 도착했다.

det.korean: ③ for the first time in its history — 역사상 처음.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 일치: for the first time in its history
❌ ① '쉽게' — almost impossible이므로 어려웠음
❌ ② '처음부터' — When James found out(나중에 알게 됨)
❌ ④ '떠나기 전에' — Not long after James had left(떠난 후)
det.tip: for the first time in its history = 역사상 처음으로

questions.passage: Two brothers each secretly recommended the other for a prestigious fellowship. Despite a strict one-per-family rule, the committee was moved by their mutual selflessness and selected both. Their story showed that true success lies not only in individual achievements but also in supporting and encouraging others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: How to Win a Fellowship: Strategies for Success
The Importance of Strict Rules in Academic Programs
Sibling Rivalry: A Story of Competition
Brothers Who Chose Each Other Over Themselves

det.korean: 제목: 자신보다 서로를 선택한 형제.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ Brothers Who Chose Each Other Over Themselves: 이타심의 핵심 포착
❌ ① 전략: 형제의 행동은 전략이 아닌 진심
❌ ② 규칙의 중요성: 규칙이 깨짐
❌ ③ 형제 경쟁: 경쟁이 아닌 양보
det.tip: chose each other over themselves = 자신보다 서로를 선택 = selflessness

questions.passage: In a small town, two brothers both applied for the Spark Fellowship. Without consulting each other, each went to the committee to recommend his brother. The committee, who had a strict one-family rule, was so impressed by their selfless behavior that they broke tradition and selected both. Their story became an inspiration, showing that true success is found in lifting others up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: selfless mutual support as the foundation of genuine success
the importance of academic talent in fellowship selection
why strict rules should never be modified for individuals
the competitive advantages of growing up with siblings

det.korean: 주제: 진정한 성공의 기반으로서의 이타적 상호 지원.
det.analysis:
✅ ① selfless mutual support: 형제의 상호 추천 → 교훈의 핵심
❌ ② 학문적 재능: 재능보다 이타심이 포인트
❌ ③ 규칙 불변: 규칙이 수정됨
❌ ④ 형제 경쟁 이점: 경쟁이 아닌 양보
det.tip: lifting others up = 타인을 끌어올리는 것. 글의 교훈 = 이타적 지원

questions.passage: Not long after James had left, Daniel showed up at the selection committee and advocated for his brother, saying "James' leadership and vision make him the perfect choice. <u>He deserves this chance more than I do.</u>"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'He deserves this chance more than I do.'가 함축하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Daniel은 자신이 프로그램에 적합하지 않다고 생각한다.
Daniel은 형의 자격을 자신보다 높이 평가하며 기회를 양보하려 한다.
Daniel은 위원회의 결정에 불만을 품고 있다.
Daniel은 James와의 경쟁에서 져서 실망하고 있다.

det.korean: Daniel은 형이 자신보다 이 기회를 더 받을 자격이 있다며 양보하는 것.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 형의 자격을 높이 평가하며 양보: 이타심의 직접적 표현
❌ ① 적합하지 않다: 자기 부정이 아니라 형에 대한 존경
❌ ③ 불만: 감사와 양보의 맥락
❌ ④ 경쟁에서 짐: 경쟁이 아닌 상호 추천
det.tip: He deserves... more than I do = 그가 나보다 더 자격이 있다. 자기희생/양보의 표현

questions.passage: Without Daniel knowing, James went to the selection committee. He told the committee, "Daniel has always been the more dedicated and talented one. He will excel in this program like no one else." Meanwhile, Daniel had the same idea as <u>his</u> older brother. He believed that his brother was the more ideal and deserving candidate. He also decided to visit and speak to the committee.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'his'가 가리키는 것은?

det.korean: 'his'는 Daniel의 소유격. 'Daniel had the same idea as his older brother(James)'.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Daniel: 문장의 주어 Daniel의 소유격. Daniel의 형 = James
❌ ① committee: 사람이 아닌 단체
❌ ③ James: James는 older brother로 지칭되는 대상
❌ ④ no one else: 앞 문장의 비교 대상
det.tip: 소유격 지칭: 'Daniel had the same idea as his older brother' → his = Daniel의

questions.passage: This posed a challenge to the selection committee, who thought it almost impossible to choose between the two equally impressive candidates. The committee gathered together, struggling all day long to decide. When James found out about this rule, <u>he</u> tried to seek a way to demonstrate Daniel's exceptional talent. Not long after James had left, Daniel showed up and advocated for his brother. The committee was deeply moved by their mutual selflessness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'he'가 가리키는 것은?

det.korean: 'he'는 규칙을 알게 된 James.
det.analysis:
✅ ① James: 'When James found out... he tried...' → he = James
❌ ② Daniel: Daniel은 demonstrate의 대상
❌ ③④ 위원장/위원: 문맥에 언급 없음
det.tip: 대명사 추적: When James found out → he = James (주어 연결)

questions.passage: He also decided to visit and speak to the committee. However, the program had a strict rule: only one family member could be selected in the same year. This posed a challenge to the selection committee, who thought it almost impossible to choose between the two equally impressive candidates. The committee gathered together, struggling all day long to decide. When James found out about this rule, he tried to seek a way to demonstrate Daniel's exceptional talent to the selection committee. Not long after James had left, Daniel showed up at the selection committee and advocated for his brother, saying "James' leadership and vision make him the perfect choice. He deserves this chance more than I do." Moved by their selflessness, the committee made an exception by selecting both brothers in the same year, for the first time in its history. Their story inspired others, showing that true success lies not only in individual achievements but also in supporting and encouraging others.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"위원회는 형제의 이타심에 감동받아 같은 해에 두 형제를 모두 선발하는 __________을 만들었다."

det.korean: 위원회는 예외(exception)를 만들었다.
det.analysis: ✅ exception: 'made an exception by selecting both brothers'에서 직접 확인
det.tip: make an exception = 예외를 만들다. for the first time in its history = 역사상 처음

questions.passage: Their story inspired others, showing that true success lies not only in individual achievements but also in __________ (support) and encouraging others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 타인을 돕고(supporting) 격려하는 데에도 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ supporting: in + -ing (전치사 + 동명사). in supporting and encouraging = 돕고 격려하는 데에
det.tip: 전치사(in) + 동명사(-ing): in supporting = 돕는 데에. and로 병렬 (supporting and encouraging)

questions.passage: Not long after James had left, Daniel showed up at the selection committee and advocated for his brother. The committee was deeply impressed. Moved by their selflessness, the committee made an exception by selecting both brothers in the same year, __________.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[for / the / first / time / in / its / history]
questions.wa: for the first time in its history
accept: for the first time in its history
For the first time in its history
for the first time in its history.

det.korean: 역사상 처음으로.
det.analysis: ✅ for the first time in its history: for the first time(처음으로) + in its history(역사에서)
det.tip: for the first time = 처음으로. in its history = 그것의 역사에서

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 빈칸을 채우시오.

"Daniel은 James 몰래 같은 생각을 가지고 있었다."
→ Daniel had __________ as his older brother.

det.korean: Daniel은 형과 같은 생각(the same idea)을 가지고 있었다.
det.analysis: ✅ the same idea: had the same idea as = ~와 같은 생각을 가지다
det.tip: the same + 명사 + as = ~와 같은. had the same idea as his older brother

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 빈칸을 채우시오.

"그는 이 기회를 나보다 더 받을 자격이 있다."
→ He __________ this chance more than I do.

det.korean: 그는 이 기회를 나보다 더 받을 자격이 있다(deserves).
det.analysis: ✅ deserves: deserve + 목적어 = ~을 받을 자격이 있다. He(3인칭 단수) + deserves
det.tip: deserve: ~을 받을 자격이 있다. He deserves this = 그는 이것을 받을 자격이 있다
